subject: Hosted API: Erasures & retention operations playbook
messages:
From: Sofia Diaz <sofia.diaz@helixcorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: security@helixcorp.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API - data geography, retention and erasure RFI

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the platform overview yesterday. Our security team compiled a short RFI focused on data residency, retention and deletion for Redwood's hosted API. Can you please: (1) confirm where customer-requested inference data and associated metadata are stored by default, (2) list default retention periods for request logs, model inputs, embeddings and backups, and (3) describe the erasure process (how a tenant/data subject can request deletion and how quickly data is purged across live caches, object stores and backups).

We attached a spreadsheet with the question IDs. Quick asks:
- Are there region options (US / EU) at tenant-level?
- What's the SLA for a deletion/erasures request?
- Do you provide evidence/artifacts (audit log entries, deletion receipts)?

Appreciate concise answers and any playbook you can share.

Attachment: Helix_RFI_questions_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Sofia Diaz
Head of Security Operations
HelixCorp

Subject: Re: Hosted API - data geography, retention and erasure RFI

Hi Sofia — thanks for sending the RFI (received). I'm looping in Kimberly (security/legal ops) and Neha (product / data ops) so we can provide an operational answer and a short playbook.

Short answer summary (high level):
- Default storage region: tenant data for hosted API is stored in the selected cloud region at signup (US or EU). By default US region is used for accounts created in North America; EU option is available and we can help you pin tenancy.
- Retention: short-lived inference caches are ephemeral (minutes-hours); request metadata/logs default to 30 days; model inputs/outputs are not stored persistently unless customer enables usage analytics or logging — when enabled, default is 30 days. Backups/snapshots: 90 days.
- Deletion: we support tenant-level erase API + documented playbook. Typical hard purge completion window is 24–72 hours for live stores, backups within the next backup window (up to 72 hours). We provide deletion receipts and audit log evidence.

I'll attach the filled spreadsheet and our internal playbook (redacted for sensitive ops details). Kimberly will add a couple of precise SLA numbers and evidence pointers.

Attachments: [helix_rfi_filled.xlsx], [redwood-erasures-playbook.pdf]

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security & Compliance

On Tue, Aug 17, 2026 at 11:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll attach the filled spreadsheet and our internal playbook (redacted for sensitive ops details). Kimberly will add a couple of precise SLA numbers and evidence pointers.

Sofia — a few clarifications / commitments from an operations SLA standpoint:

1) Regions and tenancy
- Tenant pinning: Customer can choose US or EU region at onboarding; we can create a region-bound tenant for HelixCorp (no cross-region replication for tenant data unless customers opt in).

2) Retention by default (hosted API, non-dedicated):
- Request metadata & usage metrics: 30 days (configurable by request for enterprise accounts).
- Model inputs/outputs: Not persisted by default. If logging is enabled by the customer (for analytics or debugging), default retention is 30 days.
- Streaming/long-lived KV cache: Ephemeral; entries expire after 12 hours by default unless your workload config extends TTL.
- Backups / snapshot exports: 90 days; backups are encrypted and retained for compliance purposes.

3) Deletion / erasure flow (ops playbook):
- Customer trigger: DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data (or via Console request ticket).
- Soft-delete: On request, we mark tenant objects for deletion and remove access immediately.
- Hard purge: Live stores (object/DB) are purged within 24 hours; caches are invalidated within seconds to minutes; backup snapshots are removed/de-referenced in the next scheduled purge cycle (within 72 hours).
- Evidence: We provide an audit package (deletion receipt, timestamps, storage object IDs, and an immutable audit log entry).

4) Backups & disaster recovery considerations
- Backups are stored encrypted with separate KMS keys. We can exclude customer-specific backups on request but that will affect DR SLA.

5) Audit trail retention
- Admin/audit logs (who initiated deletion, API caller identity, ops actions): 365 days by default and available via console/export.

I'll leave technical retention specifics (S3 path naming, snapshot lifecycle rules) to Neha in case you need them for your evidence pack.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park

Sofia — final consolidated response and links (per your spreadsheet IDs). Attaching the filled RFI and a short ops playbook PDF that outlines the steps we take and the artifacts we provide. Highlights below (please reference attached spreadsheet for question IDs):

Q1. Where is data stored?- Tenant data (request metadata, customer-enabled logs, and any customer opt-in artifacts) is stored in the cloud region selected at tenant onboarding (US: us-central / EU: eu-west). We do not replicate tenant data across regions unless explicitly configured via a cross-region add-on.

Q2. Default retention values (hosted API):
- Request metadata & anonymized usage metrics: 30 days (default).
- Model inputs/outputs: Not stored persistently by default. If logging is enabled by the customer, retention defaults to 30 days.
- Ephemeral KV caches: default TTL 12 hours; automatic invalidation on delete.
- Embeddings stored via our embeddings API (customer choice): retained 30 days by default unless customer sets a custom TTL or opts into longer-storage features.
- Backups/snapshots: retained 90 days; snapshots are rotated and deleted per lifecycle rules.
- Audit/admin logs: retained 365 days.

Q3. Deletion / Erasure process (what happens when you request purge):
- How to request: API: DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/data or open a support ticket with "Erase request - <tenant_id>". We also support account admin requests via Console.
- Immediate effects: access to the tenant's data is revoked immediately; tokens revoked; live caches invalidated.
- Hard purge timeline: We hard purge live object stores and DB rows within 24 hours in 90% of requests; edge cases that require manual cleanup may take up to 72 hours. Backup snapshots are removed/de-referenced during the next purge window (within 72 hours).
- Evidence provided: deletion receipt (JSON with timestamps & object IDs), immutable audit log entry with operator identity, and optional engineer sign-off if required for compliance evidence.

Q4. Evidence and attestation
- We provide an audit package as part of the erasure flow (PDF + JSON bundle) and permanent audit log entries accessible via the Console or exported to an S3/GCS location you control. We can also produce a time-bound attestation letter for enterprise agreements.

Q5. Tenant-level geo controls / region pinning
- Yes. We can pin new tenants to US or EU. For hosted API customers that require strict residency, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted tenancy pinning is available but subject to capacity confirmation.

Operational notes / caveats
- Logs and analytics: If your team enables debug-level logging or opts into long-term analytics, please be aware those artifacts are stored per the TTL you select.
- Backups & DR: If you require no backups to be kept, we can discuss a configuration but that will increase risk in DR scenarios.

Attachments included: redwood-erasures-playbook.pdf (ops steps + evidence templates), helix_rfi_filled.xlsx (your spreadsheet, answered).

If HelixCorp would like, we can schedule a short follow-up (30 mins) to walk through the playbook and provide a sample deletion receipt for a test tenant.

Regards,
